content:
alex: quick question — running into a painful edge with audit compaction + TTL for billing events.
alex: current plan: raw token events kept 30d, then compact to daily rollups stored for 365d.
alex: but what about retroactive attribution corrections that arrive at day 45+ (late provider corrections, customer disputes)?
maria: hmm, two options i see: keep a lightweight checkpointable journal for 90d OR support rehydration from object store for specific accounts.
maria: journal = small tail of raw events per tenant; rehydrate = expensive but rare. tradeoff is storage vs operator complexity.
jamal: rehydration would need deterministic compaction logic so rollups produced later match original pipeline semantics. we can't just naively replay.
jamal: also need idempotency markers: compaction must be reversible or at least patchable.
sasha: idea: keep hashes + offsets per day in rollup metadata. if a correction arrives, we verify hash mismatch and apply a delta patch that adjusts aggregates and emits an audit event.
sasha: that keeps most days immutable but makes corrections auditable.
lee: delta patches are nice but we also need monetary reconciliation: if a delta reduces a charge we need to trigger refund flow. tie to billing service.
lee: we should include a 'correction_reason' enum in the audit event: PROVIDER_CORRECTION, CUSTOMER_DISPUTE, INFERRED_RECLASSIFICATION, MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: metering-replay-job v1.4 -> staged at 03:00 UTC :eyes:
alex: what about the 30d TTL itself — should we increase to 90d to reduce rehydration frequency? cost will go up but reduces complexity.
maria: increasing retention is simplest for correctness but regresses our cost targets. maybe make retention configurable per account tier (enterprise 90d, standard 30d).
jamal: configurable retention per tenant means compaction/rollup pipeline needs a retention tag on all derived outputs and a selective compaction path. doable but adds branching.
sasha: if we do per-tenant retention, we must ensure shard routing and storage keys include retention flag to avoid mixed compaction.
lee: also remember GDPR/CCPA requests: longer retention needs stronger deletion workflows. ops/sysadmins will hate us if we forget that.
alex: ok — proposal draft: 1) keep raw events 30d by default, 2) maintain 90d lightweight per-tenant journal for premium accounts, 3) implement delta-patch mechanism for rollups + deterministic rehydrate path, 4) emit structured correction events that billing consumes.
alex: thoughts? can someone sketch the rehydrate API surface? e.g. POST /rehydrate?tenant=...&range=...
maria: sketch: POST /rehydrate {tenant, start_ts, end_ts, mode: enum{delta, full_replay}} -> returns job_id; job emits events to audit-topic and writes patches to rollup-store. idempotent.
maria: include dry_run flag for verification.
jamal: we also need a read-model migration plan for existing rollups: add metadata fields (hash, compaction_version). rolling migration is possible via background backfill.
sasha: implement compaction_version header now so new compactions are marked. older rollups treated as v0; rehydrate will upgrade to v1 when patched.
lee: timeline: P0: add correction_event schema + billing hook. P1: rehydrate API + job; P2: per-tenant retention.
jamal: risk: rehydrate load can cause storms. we should rate limit and queue per-tenant with exponential backoff.
alex: agree. Also add immutable audit events stream for external compliance (s3) with 1y TTL regardless of rollups — small digest only (hashes + metadata) to save space.
maria: that helps audits but be careful with sensitive payloads — need to redact before exporting.
sasha: put a checksum and redaction marker in the export. keep original raw in internal secure store only for 90d.
lee: action items: jamal + sasha to draft rehydrate job design; maria + alex to update billing correction schema; ops to estimate storage cost for 90d journal.
jamal: will do a design doc. aiming for RFC next week.
ops-bot: reminder set: "rehydrate design doc due" in 7 days :calendar:
